items.title: Audit all 193 git child-process call sites and reroute the unrouted ones through resolveGitCwd
items.context: Get the live list via `git grep -nE "(execFileSync|spawnSync|execSync)\(['\"']git['\"']" -- 'packages/**/*.ts'`. For each site, determine the cwd source: ALREADY routed via resolveGitCwd / resolveStorySignedWorkspace / equivalent — keep as-is. Passing projectRoot/root/metadataRoot bare — REROUTE: call resolveGitCwd at the source (or accept a resolved cwd from caller) and pass it. Be careful NOT to break the 3 ad-hoc helpers (lab.ts runGit, cli-engine.ts runGitNoThrow, declared-artifact-commit-check.ts runGit) — keep them, but ensure their CALLERS use resolveGitCwd. The two existing smokes (gitroot-cwd-routing-smoke, bare-gate-gitroot-cwd-smoke) must continue to pass. After: `npm run build` exit 0; `npm run test:e2e` ALL PASS; `npm run test:gitroot-cwd-routing` exit 0; `npm run test:bare-gate-gitroot-cwd` exit 0; wrapper-root fixture tests pass.
items.userSees: Every git call site uses a cwd obtained from resolveGitCwd (or an existing helper that itself takes a resolved cwd); both existing wrapper-root smokes still pass; build + e2e green.

happy.desc: npm run build exits 0 after reroute changes -- confirms no TS compilation errors introduced; WHY: baseline compile gate for all 9 modified files
npm run test:gitroot-cwd-routing exits 0 -- existing wrapper-root routing smoke passes byte-identically; WHY: ensures rerouted sites still produce correct cwd in wrapper-root layout
npm run test:bare-gate-gitroot-cwd exits 0 -- existing bare-gate smoke passes; WHY: ensures previously-fixed sites remain correct after bulk reroute
npm run test:e2e exits 0 -- full end-to-end suite green; WHY: no behavioral regressions in any handler/core flow that touches git

After reroute, git grep for bare-cwd sites yields 0 non-allowlisted hits: git grep -nE "(execFileSync|spawnSync|execSync)\\([\x27\x22]git[\x27\x22]" -- packages/**/*.ts piped through filter excluding allowlisted helpers yields empty; WHY: directly validates the single-choke-point invariant at source level

edge.desc: resolveGitCwd function signature at story-signed-workspace-resolution.ts is unchanged: git diff main shows the export function resolveGitCwd(...) declaration line is byte-identical or only body changes; WHY: over-reach guard per scope exclusion, no signature changes allowed

The 3 ad-hoc helpers still exist with unchanged signatures: lab.ts runGit, cli-engine.ts runGitNoThrow, declared-artifact-commit-check.ts runGit -- verified via grep for declarations; WHY: over-reach guard, plan says preserve wrappers
Total git call-site count after reroute is >= 193: git grep -c for exec.*git across packages/**/*.ts | sum; WHY: ensures no call sites were accidentally deleted instead of rerouted

adversarial.desc: Inject a bare-cwd regression line (execFileSync git with cwd:projectRoot) into a non-allowlisted file, then run test:gitroot-cwd-routing -- smoke STILL passes (it tests specific sites, not global invariant); but a global grep for bare-cwd sites now shows >=1 hit; WHY: proves existing smokes alone are insufficient to catch new regressions, motivating CHK-002 contract

Attempt to import resolveGitCwd from wrong internal path (not the public barrel export) in a new .ts file -- npm run build must fail with cannot-find-module; WHY: ensures the choke-point cannot be silently bypassed by importing from internal module paths

items.title: Add the grep-contract smoke test that fails on any bare-projectRoot git call
items.context: Create packages/main/src/tasks/gitroot-cwd-contract-smoke.ts that runs the canonical grep across `packages/**/*.ts` looking for `(execFileSync|spawnSync|execSync)\(['\"']git['\"']` and inspects each hit. The smoke FAILS if any hit's cwd argument is a bare projectRoot/root/metadataRoot identifier or string literal not sourced from resolveGitCwd. An allowlist file (or inline whitelist) is supported for the resolveGitCwd helper itself and the 3 existing helper wrappers (lab.ts runGit / cli-engine.ts runGitNoThrow / declared-artifact-commit-check.ts runGit) — any other site fails the contract. Register `test:gitroot-cwd-contract` script in root package.json and packages/main/package.json. Add an entry to the main e2e suite or run it in CI so the contract gate runs on every PR. After: `npm run test:gitroot-cwd-contract` passes on current state (after CHK-001 reroutes); intentionally introducing a regression (add `execFileSync('git',['status'],{cwd:projectRoot})` in a test fixture file) makes the smoke FAIL with a clear error pointing at the bad site.
items.userSees: `npm run test:gitroot-cwd-contract` passes on HEAD; running it after a deliberate regression injection fails with a clear pointer to the offending file:line and a remediation message naming resolveGitCwd.

happy.desc: npm run test:gitroot-cwd-contract exits 0 on HEAD (after CHK-001 reroutes are in place) -- the smoke finds zero violations; WHY: confirms contract smoke correctly passes when all sites are routed
The smoke script is wired in root package.json: jq .scripts["test:gitroot-cwd-contract"] package.json returns a non-null command; WHY: confirms npm script registration

The smoke script is wired in packages/main/package.json: jq .scripts["test:gitroot-cwd-contract"] packages/main/package.json returns a non-null command; WHY: confirms inner-package script registration

Deliberate regression injection: temporarily add execFileSync(git,[status],{cwd:projectRoot}) to a non-allowlisted .ts file, run npm run test:gitroot-cwd-contract -- exits non-zero with output containing the offending file:line and the word resolveGitCwd in the remediation message; WHY: confirms the contract actually catches regressions

edge.desc: The smoke processes its own inline known-bad fixture row and reports it as a violation (self-test) -- run the smoke with a flag or inspect its source to confirm it includes at least one known-bad fixture that it catches; WHY: ensures the smoke is not trivially passing because of an empty allowlist or empty grep results

Allowlist includes exactly the expected entries: story-signed-workspace-resolution.ts (resolveGitCwd definition), lab.ts (runGit), cli-engine.ts (runGitNoThrow), declared-artifact-commit-check.ts (runGit) -- no more, no fewer; WHY: allowlist inflation defeats the contract

The smoke file packages/main/src/tasks/gitroot-cwd-contract-smoke.ts exists and is executable via node packages/main/dist/tasks/gitroot-cwd-contract-smoke.js after build; WHY: confirms the smoke is a standalone runnable, not just a library module

Running the smoke on an empty or non-existent packages dir (e.g., from a temp dir with no .ts files) -- smoke exits 0 with no violations (vacuous pass, not crash); WHY: boundary condition for repos where grep returns nothing

adversarial.desc: Remove the entire allowlist from the smoke source (empty it), then run -- smoke MUST fail because resolveGitCwd definition site and the 3 helpers would now be flagged as violations; WHY: proves the allowlist is load-bearing and the smoke does not have a backdoor pass-all path

Add a bare-cwd git call using a VARIABLE ALIAS (e.g., const root = projectRoot; execFileSync(git,[status],{cwd:root})) -- smoke should still catch it OR the contract documentation explains this is a known limitation of grep-based analysis; WHY: adversarial evasion test for indirect references

Add a new site that is allowlisted but does NOT use resolveGitCwd (forge an allowlist entry) -- smoke passes, but git diff of the allowlist shows the addition, making it reviewable; WHY: tests that allowlist changes are visible in code review (the contract enforcement is both automated + review-gated)

Run the contract smoke after reverting CHK-001 reroutes (simulate a full regression to pre-story state) -- smoke MUST fail with multiple violations listing specific file:line entries; WHY: confirms the smoke would have caught the original 193-site problem
